content: <thought>Based on the measured resistances, the simplest network that matches all three values is a series connection of two resistors between X1 and X2 with a junction node N_b1. The resistance between X1 and N_b1 is 5 Ω (R1) and between N_b1 and X2 is 13.333 Ω (R2). Their series sum gives the measured X1‑X2 resistance of 18.333 Ω. The third resistor (R3) does not affect these measurements, so it can be placed elsewhere (e.g., between X1 and a dummy node) without influencing the terminal resistances. One resistor is twice another; we can set R3 = 10 Ω (twice R1) and connect it to a dummy node D that is not part of the X1‑X2 path. This satisfies the “three resistors total” condition while keeping the measured values unchanged.
